key_insight: A founder-enriched ADAP1 frameshift variant was strongly associated with serious mental illness, showing a rare variant can have a major transdiagnostic effect across schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests that genetically informed risk stratification and phenotype interpretation for serious mental illness may benefit from considering population-specific founder variants, not only common polygenic risk.
method: Exome sequencing of 21,958 cases and 19,826 controls from the Mision Origen biobank in a Colombian Paisa founder population.
Association testing of predicted deleterious variants across serious mental illness diagnoses.
Electronic health record NLP and neurocognitive testing to compare symptom profiles in variant carriers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports transdiagnostic associations in seven genes, with the strongest signal being a genome-wide significant ADAP1 frameshift variant that increased risk for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder by more than threefold.
watch_item: Findings come from a specific founder population, so effect sizes and variant frequencies may not generalize directly to other ancestries or clinical settings.
paper_title: A founder population reveals genetic variation with major effect on serious mental illness
